claims.source_quote_ar: لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْهُدى
claims.claim_ar: استعمال لَوْ مع لِـ في تركيب افتراضي (لو … لَ) للدلالة على حالٍ افتراضية مستحيلة أو غير محققة ويؤدي إلى تأكيد استحالة تلبية الطلب.
claims.claim_en: Use of the counterfactual conditional (لو ... لَ) to express an unreal/hypothetical situation and thereby emphasize the impossibility of granting what is demanded.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted commentary example is from a different verse/context (discussing لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ...) rather than an explicit exegesis of S6:58; the claim extrapolates the general rhetorical force of لو...ل to this ayah and should be checked against direct commentators on S6:58.

claims.claim_ar: افتتاح الكلام بفعل إنشائي/أمري (قُلْ) كأداة إنشائية تدخّل على كلام النبي موجهًا له أن يلفت القلوب إلى الافتراض ثم النفي؛ أي توظيف أسلوب الإنشاء للأمر بالكلام.
claims.claim_en: Opening the statement with an performative/imperative (قُلْ) functions as an act of injunction—an inchoative/performative device—directing the Prophet to state the hypothetical and its negation; this is the use of a performative/injunctive style.
claims.needs_review_reason: Support comes from a commentary substring using an imperative (فَافْعَل) in a related exegetical example rather than a direct gloss of قُلْ in this specific ayah; the functional match is plausible but should be verified with direct comments on S6:58.

claims.claim_ar: توفر إيجاز بلاغي عبر حذف عناصر مُ يفهَمة (حذف جواب «أن») يؤدي إلى إيجاز التعبير وإيهام الاختصار في المعنى الدالّ.
claims.claim_en: A rhetorical concision (ijaaz) effected by omission (e.g., omission of an expected reply/particle), producing compressed expression and implied meaning rather than explicit wording.
claims.needs_review_reason: The chunk mentions the phenomenon 'حذف جواب «أن»' in a different exegetical context; whether S6:58 specifically relies on this type of omission (and which element is omitted) needs confirmation from direct commentary on this ayah.
